scope: Proposition 2.1 (Finite-volume certificate) of the manuscript “Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three” (preprints/Absolutely-Continuous-Spectrum-for-Weak-Disorder-Anderson-Models-in-Dimensions-at-Least-Three-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 261 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0d971c56f6ba1641), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each fixed d ≥ 3 there exist λ0(d) > 0 and constants c, C > 0 with the following property. For every fixed 0 < λ < λ0(d), every E ∈ Id, and every m ≥ 4n0, one can use auxiliary independent randomness to construct an event Sm, depending on the fixed E, λ, such that P(Sm) → 1 as m → ∞. On Sm there are a set A ⊂ TL, |A| ≥ N/2, and complex numbers ri, i ∈ A, satisfying |ri| ≤ C, c ≤ ℑri ≤ C, such that b G = (Hm − E − η diagA r)−1 exists, ℑ b Gii ≥ c (i ∈ A). For fixed d the constants are independent of E, λ, m, and the convergence in probability is uniform in E ∈ Id for each fixed λ. The failure estimates are also uniformly small for all m ≥ 4n0 and u ∈ (1/4, 1] once n0 is sufficiently large. The potential in Hm consists entirely of the original true variables.
